useCases.title: Schema Change Detection
useCases.value: Unauthorized DDL changes to production databases can break applications. Detection ensures change control compliance.

useCases.title: Database User and Privilege Change Audit
useCases.value: New users, role grants, or privilege changes can indicate compromise or policy violation. Auditing supports compliance (SOX, PCI) and security investigations.

useCases.title: Database Audit Log Tampering Detection

useCases.title: Okta User Lifecycle Events (Provisioning / Deprovisioning)

useCases.title: SOX Access Control Audit

useCases.title: Deploy Approval Bypass Detection

useCases.title: Unauthorized Change Detection
useCases.value: Changes executed without approval or outside policy create audit exposure and outage risk; detecting them early supports SOC-2/ITIL controls and rapid rollback decisions.

useCases.title: PCI-DSS 10.3 — Audit log integrity: tampering/deletion detection on CDE log source
useCases.value: A cleared Windows Security log on a CDE host is a near-certain indicator of attacker presence. Closing the detection gap to 10 minutes saves forensics time.

useCases.title: PCI-DSS 10.7 — Log retention: CDE data-source retention + immutability attestation
useCases.value: Prevents the audit-killing discovery that retention was silently reduced during an index rebuild. Daily attestation beats the quarterly spot-check.

useCases.title: SOX-ITGC AccessMgmt.Provisioning — Financial-system user provisioning SLA & workflow adherence
useCases.value: Closes the #1 SOX deficiency 'access provisioned without an approved ticket'. Internal audit gets a daily report rather than a quarterly spot-check.

useCases.title: SOX-ITGC AccessMgmt.Termination — Deprovisioning SLA after HR termination event
useCases.value: The most common SOX finding — ex-employees retaining access — becomes measurable hour-by-hour.

useCases.title: SOX-ITGC ChangeMgmt.Testing — Financial-system change test-evidence completeness
useCases.value: Converts a common sampling control into full-coverage evidence, reducing audit sampling and cost.

useCases.title: SOX-ITGC ChangeMgmt.Approval — Segregation of duties in financial-system change approval
useCases.value: Eliminates the two patterns that SOX auditors most frequently cite. The daily report is the control evidence.

useCases.title: SOX-ITGC Operations.JobSchedule — Batch-schedule monitoring: financial-job exception visibility
useCases.value: Makes the typically-spreadsheet-based batch monitoring queryable — Ops has a live queue, auditors have a history.

useCases.title: Audit-log continuity: detect indexing gap indicating lost evidence
useCases.value: Without continuous audit logs, compliance claims are unfalsifiable. Auditors across GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, and SOX all treat log-gaps as a finding. This UC lets a customer show the auditor a gr…

useCases.title: Log tamper detection via write-once-read-many chain-of-custody
useCases.value: Produces defensible chain-of-custody evidence: auditors can be shown a 30-day view in which every bucket was either green or had a timestamped remediation ticket.

useCases.title: Log signing chain integrity — cryptographic signature drift on evidence archive
useCases.value: Replaces the quarterly 'we sampled 10 logs and checked hashes' audit procedure with a continuous control whose output is either 'zero breaks for the period' or a named remediation record. This is the…

useCases.title: Privileged session recording — missing recordings for elevated sessions
useCases.value: Converts 'we have PAM' into 'we can prove every privileged session was recorded' — the question auditors actually ask.

useCases.title: Break-glass account usage review with mandatory post-use approval
useCases.value: Break-glass misuse is the most audited sub-case of privileged access; a missing approval is a textbook SOX-ITGC deficiency.

useCases.title: Periodic access review SLA — stale certifications by control owner
useCases.value: Access review is the #1 ITGC deficiency in typical public-company audits; turning it into a green/red KPI changes the operating rhythm.

useCases.title: Standing-privilege credential vaulting drift — admin accounts outside PAM
useCases.value: Replaces the quarterly 'access-review export + spreadsheet join' with a daily evidence feed.

useCases.title: High-risk privileged-session command without JIT approval
useCases.value: Makes 'we require JIT approval for dangerous commands' an observable, always-on control.

useCases.title: Key custodian SoD — same identity creates AND approves a key
useCases.value: Provides daily evidence of key-custodian SoD rather than the common annual sample.

useCases.title: Unauthorized production change — no approved CR matches the observed change
useCases.value: Replaces the standard quarterly-sample audit with continuous evidence of the authorisation gate.

useCases.title: Change rollback execution evidence — declared rollback vs actual
useCases.value: Turns rollback-plan existence from a documentation artefact into a tested capability.

useCases.title: CAB approval bypass — change pushed before scheduled window
useCases.value: Turns CAB approval from a calendar event into an operational control with per-change evidence.

useCases.title: Backup completeness — unprotected workloads with regulated data
useCases.value: Coverage gaps are the single most common backup finding at audit; continuous evidence eliminates surprise findings.

useCases.title: Repeat audit findings — same control deficiency across consecutive audit cycles
useCases.value: Converts the 'prior year issue' anecdote into a quantitative signal.

useCases.title: Evidence-pack drift — auditor-facing vs pre-production evidence
useCases.value: Protects the integrity of the evidence that underpins the external audit.

useCases.title: Segregation of duties — toxic role combinations in IAM
useCases.value: SoD failures are the top SOX ITGC finding in the Fortune-1000 cohort; automating them is the only defensible posture.

useCases.title: SoD violations via break-glass usage — emergency role abuse
useCases.value: Break-glass is often abused to step around SoD; this UC catches that pattern without waiting for audit.

useCases.title: Developer-to-production SoD — same developer submits AND approves merge
useCases.value: Makes a core deployment-pipeline SoD requirement a continuously-enforced technical control.

useCases.title: Financial SoD — same identity posts AND approves a journal entry
useCases.value: Provides continuous evidence of a universally-audited SOX control.

useCases.title: Vendor-master SoD — same identity creates vendor AND approves payment
useCases.value: Continuously enforces a control most organisations only sample.

useCases.title: Litigation-hold override audit — holds applied/released without ticket
useCases.value: Prevents silent tampering with evidence preservation.
